questionText:
Let $G$ be a connected undirected weighted graph. Consider the following two statements.

$S_1$: There exists a minimum weight edge in $G$ which is present in every minimum spanning tree of $G$.
$S_2$: If every edge in $G$ has distinct weight, then $G$ has a unique minimum spanning tree.

Which one of the following options is correct?
explanation:
Analysis of Statement $S_1$:
Consider a graph $G$ with 3 vertices forming a triangle where all 3 edges have equal weight $1$ (which is the minimum weight). Any minimum spanning tree (MST) will select 2 edges. There are 3 distinct MSTs, and no single edge appears in all of them. Thus, $S_1$ is false.

Analysis of Statement $S_2$:
It is a fundamental property of graphs that if all edge weights in a connected undirected graph are distinct, then the graph contains a unique minimum spanning tree. Thus, $S_2$ is true.

Hence, $S_1$ is false and $S_2$ is true.
